name: Medium Engineering Team
description: A medium-scale engineering team template for growing companies (100-1000 employees). This template covers a 10-30 FTE engineering department with an Engineering Manager, Tech Lead, 4-8 Senior Engineers, 2-4 Junior Engineers, a DevOps Engineer, a QA Lead, and a GPO pod. It supports multi-team structures with sprint planning, architectural review processes, code review gates, automated testing, and on-call rotations. Designed for organizations that need structure alongside agility, with clear quality gates and cross-team coordination mechanisms.

agents.name: Engineering Manager
agents.description: People manager responsible for team health, capacity planning, performance reviews, and cross-team alignment. Ensures delivery commitments are met and removes organizational blockers.

agents.name: Tech Lead
agents.description: Senior technical authority who drives architectural decisions, conducts architectural reviews, mentors senior engineers, and ensures technical alignment across teams.

agents.name: Senior Engineer
agents.description: Experienced engineer who owns significant system components, leads feature development, performs code reviews, and contributes to architectural decisions. May serve as team lead for specific subsystems.

agents.name: Junior Engineer
agents.description: Early-career engineer implementing well-scoped features, fixing bugs, writing tests, and growing into system design under the guidance of senior team members.

agents.name: DevOps Engineer
agents.description: Infrastructure specialist responsible for CI/CD pipelines, cloud infrastructure, monitoring, and reliability engineering. Manages on-call rotation and implements SLOs.

agents.name: QA Lead
agents.description: Quality assurance leader responsible for testing strategy, test automation, quality gates, and ensuring release readiness. Defines quality standards and manages the QA process across teams.

agents.name: Engineering GPO Pod
agents.description: A pod of GPO agents handling operational support across the engineering department. Manages environment provisioning, documentation, reporting, and ad-hoc operational tasks.

workflows.name: Sprint Planning Workflow
workflows.description: Structured sprint planning process for the engineering team with capacity planning, story estimation, and commitment setting across the iteration.

config.description: Review and prioritize the product backlog, refine story estimates, ensure acceptance criteria are clear and testable
Calculate team capacity accounting for PTO, holidays, meetings, and the 20% buffer for unplanned work and on-call duties
Team commits to sprint goals based on capacity. Assign epic-level owners and distribute stories across team members
Break stories into subtasks with clear definitions of done. Ensure each task is completable within 1-2 days
Identify technical risks, dependencies on other teams, and items requiring architectural review before sprint start
Send sprint kickoff with goals, commitments, risk register, and burndown dashboard to the team and stakeholders

workflows.name: Code Review with Quality Gates
workflows.description: Multi-stage code review process with automated quality gates including security scanning, performance checks, and architectural compliance review.

config.description: Run automated checks: linting, unit tests, integration tests, SAST security scan, dependency vulnerability scan, and performance benchmark
Peer reviewer examines code for correctness, readability, edge cases, and adherence to coding standards
Tech Lead reviews for architectural alignment, pattern consistency, performance implications, and security considerations on non-trivial changes
QA Lead validates that automated test coverage meets thresholds, new test cases are included, and no regression detected
Author addresses all requested changes from peer review, architectural compliance, and QA feedback
Engineering Manager grants final merge approval after confirming all gates passed and no outstanding blockers

workflows.name: Deployment Pipeline Workflow
workflows.description: Automated deployment pipeline with multi-stage promotion from staging to production, including release validation gates.

config.description: Build application artifacts, run security scans, package Docker images, and push to the container registry with version tagging
Deploy to staging environment with canary rollout; run full integration test suite and smoke tests
QA Lead validates release candidates with regression testing, performance testing, and user acceptance criteria check
Tech Lead signs off on staging deployment confirming feature completeness, performance, and security compliance
Execute production deployment with blue-green or canary strategy; monitor error rates and latency during rollout
Run post-deployment verification: health checks, synthetic transactions, and alert monitoring; notify stakeholders of deployment status

workflows.name: Incident Response with Severity Levels
workflows.description: Structured incident response process with severity-based escalation paths, on-call management, and post-mortem culture.

config.description: Automated monitoring or user report triggers incident classification by severity: P1 (complete outage), P2 (major degradation), P3 (minor issue), P4 (cosmetic)
On-call engineer acknowledges and activates the incident response channel. For P1/P2, Engineering Manager is paged and assigned as incident commander
Investigation team diagnoses root cause using logs, metrics, and traces. Implements immediate mitigation (rollback, feature flag, scaling) while deeper investigation continues
Send status updates to stakeholders at regular intervals (P1: every 15 minutes, P2: every 30 minutes, P3: every hour) with current status, impact, and ETA
Implement permanent fix, deploy to production, verify service health through automated checks and manual validation
Schedule blameless post-mortem within 5 business days for P1/P2 incidents. Assign action items with owners and due dates

workflows.name: Post-Mortem Workflow
workflows.description: Blameless post-incident review process that drives learning and prevents recurrence through actionable follow-up items.

config.description: Collect all incident data: timeline from monitoring, chat logs, deployment records, metrics snapshots, and user impact reports
Schedule blameless post-mortem meeting with all involved parties within 5 business days. Send pre-read with incident timeline
Facilitate blameless post-mortem: review timeline, identify contributing factors, discuss what went well and what did not, focus on system issues not individual blame
Write post-mortem document with root cause analysis, timeline, impact assessment, contributing factors, and actionable recommendations
Convert recommendations into specific action items with owners, priority levels, and due dates. Categorize as prevent, detect, respond, or recover
Track all action items to completion. Review progress in regular team meetings. Report on post-mortem closure rate in monthly quality review

workflows.name: Architectural Review Workflow
workflows.description: Formal architectural review process for significant design changes, new system integrations, and infrastructure modifications.

config.description: Submit EDesign Artifact (eSignal) with proposed change description, alternatives considered, impact analysis, and rollback plan
Tech Lead performs initial review for completeness, feasibility, and alignment with architectural principles
Two senior engineers review the design for technical soundness, scalability, security implications, and performance considerations
Conduct architectural review meeting with stakeholders. Present design, discuss concerns, and document decisions and trade-offs
Implement the approved design following standard feature development workflow with regular sync-ups on architectural concerns
Verify that the implementation matches the approved architectural design. Close the eSignal with implementation notes and lessons learned

semantic_memory.description: Stores structured knowledge about architecture decisions, coding standards, debugging patterns, and system behavior across the engineering organization

episodic_memory.description: Records incident timelines, deployment histories, sprint outcomes, and review decisions for retrospectives and learning

procedural_memory.description: Caches successful operational procedures, deployment scripts, troubleshooting sequences, and automation patterns

graph_memory.description: Maps service dependencies, team ownership boundaries, and knowledge relationships for understanding blast radius and escalation paths

immutable_storage.description: Git commit history, deployment audit logs, and architectural decision records provide the immutable record of all changes

governance_rules.name: Multi-Gate Code Review
governance_rules.description: All production code must pass peer code review, architectural compliance check (for non-trivial changes), and QA validation before merging to main. No exceptions.

governance_rules.name: SLO-Driven Deployment
governance_rules.description: No production deployment may violate defined Service Level Objectives. If SLO error budgets are exhausted, deployments pause until budget is replenished or risk is accepted by Engineering Manager.

governance_rules.name: Incident Post-Mortem Requirement
governance_rules.description: All P1 and P2 incidents must have a blameless post-mortem within 5 business days. Action items must be assigned, tracked, and closed. Post-mortem reports are archived and reviewed quarterly.

governance_rules.name: Test Coverage and Quality Gates
governance_rules.description: Minimum 80% test coverage for new code and 75% for existing code. PRs that reduce coverage below baseline are rejected. Performance benchmarks must not regress.

governance_rules.name: Secrets and Credential Management
governance_rules.description: No secrets stored in version control. All credentials managed through a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault). Quarterly credential rotation required. Exposure triggers immediate rotation and incident.

governance_rules.name: On-Call Rotation Coverage
governance_rules.description: Every member of the engineering team participates in the on-call rotation. P1 incidents must be acknowledged within 15 minutes. No unassigned on-call shifts allowed.

kpis.name: Deployment Frequency
kpis.description: How often the team successfully deploys to production Measured as: count per week

kpis.name: Lead Time for Changes
kpis.description: Time from code commit to production deployment Measured as: median hours

kpis.name: Change Failure Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of deployments causing a P2 or higher production incident Measured as: percentage

kpis.name: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
kpis.description: Average time to restore service after a production incident Measured as: minutes

thresholds.target_label: less than 1 hour for P1, 4 hours for P2

kpis.name: Sprint Velocity
kpis.description: Average story points completed per sprint, tracking team delivery predictability Measured as: story points per sprint

kpis.name: Test Coverage
kpis.description: Percentage of codebase covered by automated tests Measured as: percentage

thresholds.target_label: at least 80% new code, 75% existing code

kpis.name: Bug Escape Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of defects found by users vs. caught by automated testing Measured as: percentage

operational_policies.name: On-Call Rotation Policy
operational_policies.description: All senior engineers and the DevOps Engineer participate in a weekly on-call rotation. P1 incidents require acknowledgment within 15 minutes. On-call engineers are compensated with time-off in lieu. Escalation to Engineering Manager after 30 minutes for P1.

operational_policies.name: Branching and Release Strategy
operational_policies.description: Use trunk-based development with short-lived feature branches. Main branch is protected and requires all quality gates. Release branches created from main for versioned releases. Hotfix branches for critical production fixes with expedited review.

operational_policies.name: Incident Severity and Response SLAs
operational_policies.description: P1 (Critical): Complete outage affecting all users -- respond within 15 minutes, resolve within 8 hours. P2 (High): Major feature degraded for significant users -- respond within 30 minutes, resolve within 8 hours. P3 (Medium): Minor issue with workaround -- respond within 4 hours, resolve within 2 business days. P4 (Low): Cosmetic or minor -- respond within 1 business day.
